## Intake review

Fleet-monitor intake pass (2026-10-28T02:40:00Z): this issue was missing a `priority/*` label and/or the standard `## Acceptance criteria` section and was not yet `meta/enriched`. The criteria section has been appended to the body (original text preserved verbatim above it) and labels normalized.

**Related:** Epic: #1184 (PM stack coherence design series). Siblings in the same series were intake-enriched in prior monitor runs (#1264–#1277).

**Notes:** Design-series issue (SLOs + self-healing), filed 2026-10-27 by Drew as part of the #1184 batch; body is well-formed (Why + design questions + its own Acceptance section). Still live: merged-PR search this run returns only unrelated PRs whose text coincidentally contains the number — none resolves or implements this design.

**Risks:** Design-only stall risk (see tail).

**Suggested approach:**  This is one of the #1184 PM-stack coherence design series; its own "Acceptance" section already states the bar (design note in `doc/` + implementation sub-issues), and the appended criteria restate that in the fleet's standard heading so the monitor and queue can gate on it. Risks: design-only items can sit silently — per house rules a design with no implementation link is flagged by the next sweep, so the follow-through that matters is the sub-issue filing, not the note alone. Suggested approach: answer the design questions against the current aggregator/orchestrator code (cite file:line), land the note, file the implementation sub-issues in the same pass.

body: Specialization filed: #6031 (browser-dependent quota watchdog) is this issue's remediation-catalogue pattern applied to quota sources whose only read path is a logged-in console (Mistral first). Its catalogue entries — CDP session re-validation, browser re-login via standing SSO, escalate-to-browser-agent — with attempt caps (2/rung/incident), disk-persisted cooldowns, and the never-list (no quota-data writes, no credential changes beyond re-storing a session under its registered name, allowlist origins only) are written to fold into this issue's catalogue rather than live as a parallel framework. Escalation split follows this issue's rule: remediation first, Drew only on human-blocked or failed remediation.

Released to the queue under Drew's 2026-11-13 unblock-all order (main chat, 23:53 CT). Task(s) 15157 moved from blocked/parked to queued in the fleet unblock-all pass (worker `main-unblock-all-2026-11-13`). Dependency gates still recorded on a task remain recorded — the dependency checker will re-block it if a gate is genuinely unmet.

🤖 **Agent note** · triaged
- **Agent:** queue worker (repo-worker-code), lane code-b
- **Session / ID:** task 15157 (triage of #1260)
- **Verdict:** still live. #1260 is OPEN, unheld, and the design work remains — the existing watchdog detector does not resolve it (confirming the 2026-11-03 triage note). This is a design deliverable, not a code fix: a design note in `doc/` answering the five design questions, plus implementation issues filed as sub-issues of epic #1184.
- **Triage labels:** work kind = design note (bounded doc PR); priority/normal, effort/m, kind/feature already on the issue and confirmed. Acceptance for the follow-on: the note answers every design question (per-facet freshness SLOs + error budgets, remediation catalogue with guardrails / attempt caps / cooldowns, post-remediation verification + logging, escalation thresholds, the watchdog never-do list), names every Drew question explicitly, and the implementation sub-issues exist under #1184.
- **Routing:** the packet schema (repo-task/v1) has no design kind, so the follow-on is enqueued as a `small_fix` packet scoped to exactly that doc-PR deliverable: **task 16644**. First concrete step for that task: inventory the current health page facets and the #1148 watchdog design, then draft the SLO table from live facet ages.
- **Links:** queue task 15157; follow-on task 16644; epic #1184; specialization #6031

Done: design note `doc/2026-11-14T12-54-00Z_design_pm_stack_slo_watchdog/` merged via PR #9987 (b71b7a507158c486d9063b8e67b01fc9655eabc5). All acceptance criteria met:
- All five design questions answered: per-facet SLOs with 30-day error budgets and health-page display (§1); remediation catalogue with per-action caps/cooldowns, global caps, circuit breakers, stateful services escalate-only (§2); verification against each facet's own SLO signal with an append-only journal mirrored to the actions feed (§3); budget-aware escalation — page vs NEEDS ORCHESTRATOR (§4); the never-do list plus watchdog self-failure detection (§5).
- Implementation issues filed, each with its own acceptance criteria: #9988 (SLO sampler/display), #9989 (remediation executor), #9990 (verification + journal), #9991 (escalation router), #9992 (heartbeat + self-failure checker). Native sub-issue linking to epic #1184 hit GitHub's 100 sub-issue cap on the epic (HTTP 422); they are linked from the epic by comment 6877585254 and from their own bodies instead.
- The five questions needing Drew are named explicitly in §6 of the note (page channel, SLO ratification, tunnel restarts, stateful exceptions, journal retention) — they gate implementation choices, not this design.
Closing this design issue; the follow-ons carry the work from here.
